chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one most deserving of the funeral prayer is the one who prays over the deceased, or he may command whomever he wishes.

key_terms.أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِهَا: The most deserving of the people regarding it

ai.seo_question: Who is most deserving to lead the funeral prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying the hierarchy for leading the funeral prayer, emphasizing that the primary right belongs to the person most closely connected to the deceased or the one who arranges the burial. The phrase 'or he may command whom he loves' highlights the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence, allowing the primary entitled person to delegate the role to another, reflecting the communal nature of the ritual. This ruling underscores the importance of both kinship ties and social preference in determining religious leadership during funeral rites.
